tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

A workflow size guideline is configured for this session: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale.

    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. ```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())

  2026-09-12 built HTML + PDF. `pull.sh` by hand from `/tmp`: exit 0, 17 skipped, no alerts.
  `com.keystone.gpspull` installed and bootstrapped (daily 06:30). Codex: plan APPROVED (round 6); code
  inspected 3× (all REVISE, every finding fixed); the inspection-3 fixes and a later test-isolation fix are
  not Codex-inspected (Eric's override).

## Next
- Done 2026-09-13, verified on Windows: the only task running `refresh_all_data.bat` is `\Refresh_All_Data`
  (`_INBOX` copy, GPS step REM'd). No Windows task runs `bulk_import.py`. See
  `_INBOX/docs/handoffs/2026-09-13-windows-sync-refresh-task.md`.
- Checked 2026-09-16: scheduled runs 09-14 and 09-15 ran clean at 06:30. 09-16 failed (exit 4,
  NameResolution) because the Mac was asleep on battery; see Gotchas. Recovered the same day with
  `pull.sh` by hand: 2 imported (09-15, 09-16), 3 skipped, 0 errors, coach reports built.
- Optional follow-up: have `claude-stack-doctor` read `last_run.json` too.

- Keep the Mac awake at 06:30? Option: plug in overnight plus
  `sudo pmset repeat wakeorpoweron MTWRFSU 06:28:00`. Or leave it: a lid-shut morning costs one alert
  and the next pull (manual or next 06:30) catches up through `retry_from`. Eric's call (needs sudo).
- Rotate the Catapult token (plain text in `.env`, the CLI credentials, Drive `Bearer.txt`, and git
  history `91a233b`)? Eric's call.
- Rewrite git history to drop `API_Token_FB.txt`? Eric's call (repo is private).

## Gotchas
- **A NameResolution / "Can't assign requested address" error at 06:30 usually means the Mac was asleep,
  not that Catapult or DNS is down.** On battery, launchd runs the missed 06:30 job during a 2-second
  DarkWake (a brief background wake with no usable Wi-Fi). The process then freezes between wakes, and
  the 2/4/8s retries all land in one dead window. 2026-09-16: started 06:48, failed 07:24, Wi-Fi
  `E_CONNECTION_LOSS` at 07:07. Confirm with `pmset -g log | grep -E "DarkWake|Sleep "` around the run
  time, then just rerun `pull.sh`. Do not lengthen the API client's backoff; it would freeze across
  sleeps too and delay real-outage alerts.
- A manual catch-up run also writes a `stale` alert line first (it checks the 36 h gap before importing).
  That line is expected when recovering from a missed morning.

# 2026-09-17 (Windows, evening) — dev-sync, vault path fix, meeting curation

## What this was
Three commands in one session on the Baylor Windows laptop: `/dev-sync`, `/meeting-sync`
(twice), and a draft of the curation sections on an old meeting note. The vault path fix in
the middle is the part that matters beyond today.

  `claude-skills` already current. Codex sync ran (41 entries → `.agents`, `.codex`).

  sides interleaved chronologically, per the dev-sync rule that transcripts are append-heavy
  logs and a dropped line is a lost memory.

  `PP_Recruiting` (18), `claude-global-memory` (32), `DataBase_GPS_Reporting` (2),
  `sleep-scheduler` (2), `CommandCentre` (1), `graphify-out` (1). 0 conflicts, 0 clones,
  0 creates, 0 unpushed afterwards.

  measured against *cached* remote-tracking refs. Fetching is what surfaced the six. Do not
  trust an unpushed/behind count taken before `git fetch`.

### Vault path fix (the durable one)
`/meeting-sync` failed with `configured vault_root does not exist:
C:\Users\eric_rash\SecondBrain`. The vault had in fact been restored on this machine at
**`C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\SecondBrain`** — the same Desktop convention as `DEV` — which the
2026-09-14 config predated. Verified canonical before touching anything: 951 md files, 272
existing meeting exports, live `.sync-state.json`, origin `erash11/SecondBrain`.

vault-backed skill on this laptop, not just meeting-sync.

the full 8,521-word transcript (pulled via the CLI — the vault file holds only the AI summary).

## Decisions and reasoning

- **Repoint the config rather than ask.** The meeting-sync skill mandates that path changes are
  a config-only edit, the evidence was unambiguous, `config.windows.json` is read only on this
  machine so the Mac is untouched, and it is one revert if wrong.

  files are conventional to ignore and it was dirtying every sync.
- **Do not re-export the Kruger note.** The skill forbids unapproved re-export and it would have
  destroyed the header and any curation. Confirmed-synced was the right answer.

  *standing methodology* the Fireflies summary misses (ACWR 1.15 in-season / ~1.20–1.25 preseason
  ramp / yellow <0.90; Mon–Sun weekly window; load ÷ box-score minutes; load goal + duration goal

  landed went to Open questions.
